title: Enterprise Onboarding, Health Checks & Escalation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding, recurring health checks, quarterly business reviews (QBRs), and the multi-tier escalation path. The goal is to provide a repeatable, observable approach that reduces time-to-value, surfaces operational risks early, and ensures rapid resolution when incidents impact customer SLAs.

Audience:
Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, On‑Call SREs, and Customer Engineering.

Key outcomes:
- Predictable onboarding milestones and success criteria.
- Regular health check cadence tied to quantifiable metrics.
- Clear, time-bound escalation steps for Sev1–Sev3 issues.
- Templates for QBRs and integration acceptance.

Prerequisites (Customer-side and Redwood):
| Item | Owner | Minimum required | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Dedicated point of contact (POC) | Customer | 1 | Name, role, email, preferred contact hours |
| Account-level API key | Redwood/Customer | API key provisioned | Use scoped key for initial integration |
| Networking | Customer/Infra | IP allowlist / VPN | If Private deployment: VPC peering details |
| Test dataset & example prompts | Customer | 10–50 representative prompts | Used for baseline quality checks |
| Compliance documents | Customer/Legal | Completed | Data residency/KMS requirements |

Roles & responsibilities
- Customer Success (owner): coordinates onboarding, schedules QBRs, tracks milestones.
- Solutions Engineering: integration support, initial performance tuning, quantization/model recommendations.
- Support (L1/L2): triage customer tickets, run diagnostics, escalate per playbook.
- SRE/Infra (L3): investigate runtime issues, capacity, kernel regressions, and deploy fixes.
- Security/Privacy: review compliance artifacts and approve deployments for restricted data.

Enterprise Onboarding checklist (recommended timeline: 0–8 weeks)
1. Kickoff (week 0): Introductions, goals, sample workloads, success metrics.
2. Access & networking (week 0–1): Exchange IPs, provision API keys, confirm access to staging.
3. Integration & quickstart (week 1–2): Run quickstarts (Repos: quickstarts-and-templates), validate basic inference calls, verify response formats.
4. Baseline perf & quality tests (week 2–3): Run 1k–5k requests across representative prompts; capture latency, throughput, token cost, and quality metrics.
5. Configuration & tuning (week 3–4): Apply batching, caching, and quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize. Document chosen model variant and resource profile.
6. Security & compliance review (week 3–5): Ensure KMS/HSM integration and auditing set up; sign off on retention policies.
7. Pilot (week 4–6): Customer runs a pilot at low traffic to validate behavior under production conditions.
8. Go-live & runbook handover (week 6–8): Promote config to prod, confirm SLO targets, and hand over runbooks and escalation contacts.

Integration guide (common patterns)
- Recommended flow: SDK -> Redwood API Gateway -> Routed model endpoint -> Observability hooks (tracing + logs).
- Typical environment variables / configuration (example):
| Key | Example value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | rk_live_xxx | Auth to Redwood API |
| REDWOOD_REGION | us-west-2 | Region to route requests |
| MODEL | redwood/open-13b-v1 | Model variant |
| MAX_TOKENS | 1024 | Per-request token limit |
| BATCHING_ENABLED | true | Runtime batching toggle |

Example curl quick test:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-13b-v1","input":"Summarize the following document...","max_tokens":256}'
```

Acceptance criteria for integration
- API responses within latency SLO (p50 <= 120ms p95 <= 350ms for standard routes).
- End-to-end request success rate >= 99.5% during pilot traffic.
- Quality baseline: human-evaluated pass rate >= agreed threshold (e.g., 85% on representative prompt set).

Escalation playbook (operational summary)
Severity definitions:
- Sev1 (Critical): Production outage or >25% of requests failing for a customer, or response content causing safety/regulatory violations.
- Sev2 (High): Degraded performance impacting core flows (p95 latency > 2x SLO) or frequent errors for a subset of customers.
- Sev3 (Medium): Non-urgent bugs, onboarding blockers, documentation gaps.

Escalation steps (time-bound)
- Sev1:
  1. Triage (0–10 minutes): L1/Support triages, open a ticket in support system and mark "Sev1". Notify CSM and on-call SRE via PagerDuty (PD).
  2. Notify (10–20 minutes): CSM informs customer POC with status update and ETA; Solutions Engineering joins if integration suspected.
  3. Investigate (20–60 minutes): SRE runs diagnostics (see runbook commands below), identify root cause, and apply mitigation (rollback, quorum routing, model variant fallback).
  4. Resolve & RCA (within 24–72 hours): Implement fix, perform postmortem, and share RCA with customer including timeline and corrective actions.
- Sev2:
  1. Triage (0–30 minutes): Ticket created, L2 assigned, notify CSM.
  2. Mitigate (1–4 hours): Apply temporary workarounds (reduce batch sizes, pin model version, increase capacity).
  3. Fix & follow-up (1–7 days): Schedule engineering fix and update customer.
- Sev3:
  1. Triage (same business day): L1 documents the issue and provides workaround if available.
  2. Resolve (1–30 days): Route to backlog, provide status updates during weekly syncs.

Standard diagnostics (runbook snippets)
- Check customer route health:
  - curl health endpoint: curl -s https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/routes/{route_id}/health
  - Query recent errors in logs: `logs query --service=inference --filter="route:{route_id}" --last=1h`
- Performance counters to collect:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate (RPS), GPU utilization, queue length, kernel retries, OOM counts.
- Temporary mitigations:
  - Switch routing policy to a lower-latency region or to dedicated capacity.
  - Pin to a smaller model variant or enable prefix caching.
  - Increase concurrency limits and scale up Dedicated pool.

Known issues and recommended workarounds (living list)
- Issue: Occasional tokenization mismatch for language X that truncates inputs.
  Workaround: Pre-tokenize client-side and pass as token sequence when supported; increase max_tokens by +64 during migration.
- Issue: Elevated p95 latency under specific burst patterns when batching window is large.
  Workaround: Reduce batching window from 50ms to 20ms for low-latency routes or enable dynamic batching thresholds.
- Issue: Model drift observed in weekly evals after a new model rollout.
  Workaround: Roll back to previous model variant, run eval suite on staging, and perform A/B rollout with canary percentage.

Health checks & QBR materials
Cadence:
- Weekly health check (CSM + SE): informal sync to review recent incidents, adoption metrics, and any open action items.
- Monthly technical review (SE + Infra): deeper dive into performance trends, config changes, and upcoming infra maintenance.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR): executive summary, metrics, roadmap alignment, and strategic recommendations.

Suggested QBR agenda (60–90 minutes)
1. Executive summary (5–10m): key wins, risks, and immediate asks.
2. Usage & adoption metrics (15–20m): tokens consumed, active routes, cost per 1k tokens, latency SLOs, error rates.
3. Performance & reliability (10–15m): incidents since last QBR, MTTR, capacity posture.
4. Quality & evaluations (10–15m): prompt-level regressions, eval pass rates, A/B test outcomes.
5. Roadmap & feature requests (10–15m): upcoming Redwood product changes and customer feature needs.
6. Action items & success criteria (5–10m): ownership and timelines.

Metrics to include in dashboards:
- Traffic: daily active routes, RPS per route.
- Cost: tokens per 1k, average cost per route, billing anomalies.
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, GPU utilization.
- Reliability: request success rate, number of incidents, MTTR, SLA compliance.
- Quality: eval pass rate on canonical prompt set, top failing prompts.

Templates and artifacts (links & attachments)
- Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet): use as canonical task tracker for milestones.
- QBR slide deck template: includes metrics slide, incident summary slide, roadmap slide.
- Integration test harness: quick scripts and sample dataset in quickstarts-and-templates.

Postmortem & RCA expectations
- Every Sev1 must produce a postmortem within 72 hours with: timeline, root cause, mitigations, customer impact, and follow-up actions assigned.
- Share a customer-facing summary and an internal technical RCA.

Communication guidelines with customers
- For Sev1: provide updates every 15–30 minutes until mitigation; escalate to executive sponsor for prolonged outages.
- For lower severities: set expectation for update cadence during initial triage and keep CSM looped in.
- Maintain a single source of truth (ticket URL) for status and artifacts.

Handover checklist (to CSM & Support)
- Completed runbooks and escalation contacts.
- Access to monitoring dashboards and alert subscriptions.
- Documented performance baselines and quality thresholds.
- Signed compliance artifacts if applicable.
